author: Elisa Carollo
description: Fridman Gallery's survey of the Harlem-born artist brings together quilts, paintings and prints from the 1970s to today, grouped by affinity rather than chronology. The works show how her blend of fabric, found objects and paint was ahead of its time and remains strikingly current.
title: Dindga McCannon Has Been Stitching Black History into the American Art Canon for 60 Years

author: Anders Fryxell
description: atNorth's Anders Fryxell examines how the Nordic region has emerged as a global leader in A.I.-ready digital infrastructure, at a moment when hyperscalers and enterprises are struggling to secure sustainable capacity. The Nordics’ investments in renewable energy, grid resilience and circular economy practices offer a practical blueprint for scaling A.I. without sacrificing reliability or climate goals.
title: The Nordic Blueprint for Building A.I. Infrastructure at Scale

author: Christa Terry
description: The self-taught Belgian painter's new exhibition at Sorry We're Closed in Brussels turns flea-market finds, folk imagery and everyday objects into saturated, strangely affecting still lifes. In conversation with Observer, he talks about his factory work, his debt to Philip Guston and why he resists symbolism.
title: Kristof Santy Would Rather Trust Objective Reality than Reach for Eve’s Apple

author: Dan Duray
description: The curator of Italy's 2022 Venice Biennale pavilion has returned to the museum where his career took shape after years working in Australia and Latin America. His vision for the institution includes rethinking its collection displays, broadening its funding and anchoring its program in the Mediterranean.
title: Newly Appointed Madre Director Eugenio Viola Sees the Museum as a Living Archive

author: Beth Duckett
description: Bill Gates wants to keep A.I. from becoming another technology that reaches wealthy countries first. His foundation is committing at least $1 billion to put the tools to work in clinics, classrooms and farms around the world.
title: Bill Gates Is Spending $1 Billion to Keep A.I. From Widening the Global Divide

author: Daniella Nicola
description: Thierry Stern has spent 17 years leading Patek Philippe. Now, with sons Adrien and Tristan entering the family business, he has roughly a decade to decide which one is ready to succeed him.
title: Patek Philippe Has Two Heirs and One Presidency

author: Katherine Parker-Magyar
description: With no chairlifts in sight, the only way to earn your turns in the backcountry paradise of the Sunnmøre and Romsdal Alps is to hike your way up.
title: Nordic by Nature: Ski Touring Through Norway’s Fjord Country
